articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally turned GitHub into their personal AWS credential buffet, exposing highly privileged GovCloud keys to anyone with functioning eyeballs. Because nothing says 'cybersecurity leadership' like leaving the keys to the kingdom in a public repo.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Shifting Identity Security Budget Dynamics
articles.summary: Google's API keys stay active for 23 minutes after 'deletion' despite claims of immediate termination. That's enough time to order a pizza AND steal all your cloud data—multitasking at its finest.

articles.title: Cisco used AI to write security incident reports, with mixed results
articles.summary: Trump Mobile allegedly leaked user data to anyone capable of sending an HTTP request. The bar for accessing sensitive information has never been lower—not even a CAPTCHA required.

articles.title: Megalodon GitHub Attack Targets 5,561 Repos with Malicious CI/CD Workflows
articles.summary: HackerOne slashes bug bounty payouts by 75%, proving that corporate gratitude for security research has the half-life of a mayfly. Critical vulns now worth pocket change—because who needs motivated researchers anyway?

articles.title: Local heterogeneity in Lassa fever serology in rural Nigeria: Implications for vaccine trial site selection
articles.summary: Cisco patches a perfect 10.0 CVSS flaw in Secure Workload that handed out data access like party favors. When your security product has maximum-severity bugs, irony officially flatlines.

articles.title: A Hacker Group Is Poisoning Open Source Code at an Unprecedented Scale
articles.summary: Microsoft patches two Defender zero-days already being exploited in the wild. The defender has become the defended—and it's losing badly.

articles.title: GitHub Confirms 3,800 Internal Repos Stolen Through Poisoned VS Code Extension
articles.summary: TeamPCP executes unprecedented software supply chain poisoning campaign, because apparently regular hacking wasn't chaotic enough. They're not just breaking things—they're breaking the things that build other things.

articles.title: Trump Mobile Hit With Fresh Humiliation
articles.summary: GitHub confirms 3,800 internal repositories stolen via malicious VS Code extension targeting their own employee. The irony of the world's largest code repository getting pwned through a poisoned coding tool is *chef's kiss* perfect.

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF celebrates a rare win for end-to-end encryption, because in 2026 keeping your conversations private apparently counts as a victory. Digital rights advocacy: where the bar is underground and we're still limbo dancing.

articles.title: China's Webworm Uses Discord, Microsoft Graphs to Hack EU Governments
articles.summary: EFF releases guide to fight digital surveillance normalization across the Americas, where human rights violations have become as routine as morning coffee. Time to make Big Brother uncomfortable again.
